summary: This regulation sets limits on how many board positions a director can hold at the same time in certain companies whose securities are traded on a stock exchange. It counts both regular seats and alternate seats. It also gives a specific deadline for directors to meet these limits.
points: A person must not act as a director in more than seven listed entities.
A person must not serve as an independent director in more than seven listed entities.
A person serving as a whole time director or managing director in any listed entity must serve as an independent director in not more than three listed entities.
The entity must comply with these provisions within six months from the date of publication or the date of the Annual General Meeting, whichever is later.
example: Aarav is a business professional based in Mumbai. He currently sits on the board of directors for six regular companies and two high value debt listed entities whose securities are traded on a stock exchange. Because the rule states a person may act as a director in not more than seven listed entities in total, Aarav exceeds the allowed limit. To follow the law correctly, he must resign from at least one of these directorships. Additionally, he must ensure he meets this requirement within the deadline given, which is six months from the date of publication or the date of the Annual General Meeting, whichever is later.

terms.meaning: Companies or organizations whose shares, debt, or other securities are traded on a stock exchange.
A board member who does not have a material or pecuniary relationship with the company and helps bring an impartial view.
A director who devotes their whole time of working capacity to the company.

watch: People often forget that alternate directorships and high value debt listed entities count toward the total limit.
